rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance (just cause eviction and relocation assistance)
rules.requirement: A landlord may end a covered tenancy only for an at-fault reason (e.g., nonpayment, breach, nuisance) or a no-fault reason (owner move-in, withdrawal from market, government/court order, substantial remodel or demolition), and must state the cause in the termination notice. For no-fault terminations the landlord must give relocation assistance of two months' rent (three months if the tenant is a senior 62+ or disabled), by direct payment or rent waiver.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador solo puede terminar un arrendamiento cubierto por una causa culpable (p. ej., falta de pago, incumplimiento, molestia) o sin culpa (mudanza del propietario, retiro del mercado, orden gubernamental o judicial, remodelación sustancial o demolición), y debe indicar la causa en el aviso. En terminaciones sin culpa debe dar asistencia de reubicación de dos meses de renta (tres meses si el inquilino tiene 62 años o más o tiene una discapacidad), mediante pago directo o exención de renta.
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less). Exempt: transient hotels, short stays, deed-restricted affordable housing (not Section 8 voucher holders), mobilehomes subject to MRL, certain institutional housing, owner-occupied shared housing or owner-occupied duplexes, single-family units/condos owned by non-corporate, non-REIT landlords who gave written exemption notice, and housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes).
rules.exemptions: Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); owner-occupied duplexes; owner-occupied single-family rentals of no more than two units/bedrooms; alienable single units owned by individuals (not REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member) with written exemption notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent; 3 months if tenant is senior (62+) or disabled
rules.effective_date_quote: The Ordinance goes into effect June 24, 2023.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for injunctive relief and damages including punitive damages; wrongful eviction liability of at least 3x actual economic damages; failure to pay relocation assistance liable for at least 3x the required assistance plus actual damages; attorney's fees.
rules.caveat: Secondary source (Legal Aid fact sheet updated Sept 2023); citation is to the division of the Municipal Code as described. SDHC notice-submission requirement was not yet in effect pending portal launch.

rules.title: San Diego buyout agreement disclosures and requirements
rules.requirement: Before making a buyout (cash-for-keys) offer, a landlord must give the tenant written disclosures, including the right to refuse and to consult an attorney and the relocation amount owed. A buyout for less than the relocation assistance owed is void.
rules.requirement_es: Antes de hacer una oferta de compra de salida, el arrendador debe entregar divulgaciones escritas, incluido el derecho a rechazar, a consultar a un abogado y el monto de reubicación debido. Un acuerdo por menos de la asistencia de reubicación es nulo.
rules.quoted_span: Buyout agreements for amounts less than the amount of relocation assistance available to Tenant is void.
rules.coverage_conditions: Same coverage as the Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance.
rules.effective_date_quote: The Ordinance goes into effect June 24, 2023.
rules.caveat: Secondary source; buyout rules summarized, not the ordinance text.
